Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment." He said, "The supplication of you two has been answered, so remain steadfast..."} (10:88–89).

So this hardening of the heart is the same as turning away and preventing.

For this reason Ibn 'Abbas said: "He means: prevent it. The meaning is: make it hard and seal it, so that it will not soften and will not open up to faith."

This agrees with what is in the Torah: Allah the Exalted said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh, for I will harden his heart, so that he will not believe until I show My signs and wonders in Egypt."

This hardening and making hard is part of the perfection of the Lord's justice (ʿadl) toward His enemies, for He made it a punishment for them because of their disbelief and turning away, just as He punishes them with calamities. For this reason it is praiseworthy: it is good when it comes from Him, and the most wicked thing when it comes from them, for it is justice and wisdom from Him, and it is injustice and foolishness from them. Thus divine decree (qaḍāʾ) and predestination (qadar) are the acts of a just, wise, self-sufficient, knowing Being who places good and evil in the most fitting places for them. What is decreed and predestined becomes injustice, oppression, and foolishness when it comes from the servant, and it is the act of an ignorant, unjust, foolish one.

(Section)

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways, the ways to the heavens, and look upon the God of Moses"﴾

This indicates that Moses, peace be upon him, used to say: "My God is in the heaven," while Pharaoh thought he was lying. If anyone argues against us about what we have already presented...

He also said: If it were so, it would resemble created things, because whatever is encompassed by places and contained by them is created. Something that is not bound and has no meaning... because He, the Exalted, "there is nothing like unto Him" (42:11) among His creation, and He is not compared with anything of His creatures, nor is He grasped by analogy, nor is He measured with people. He existed before places and will exist after them. There is no god but He, the Creator of all things, with no partner. The Muslims and every person of intellect agree that no existing thing can be conceived except in some place, and that what is not in a place is nonexistent. It is established by reason and proven by evidence that He existed in eternity without a place, and He is not nonexistent. How then can He be compared with anything of His creation, or be likened or assimilated to them? Exalted is Allah above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation.

If someone says: When we describe our Lord, the Exalted, as having existed in eternity without a place, and then He created places so that He became in a place, this entails our admitting change and transition, since He departed from His attribute in eternity and became in one place rather than another.

It is said to him: Likewise, you claim that He existed without a place and then became in every place. You have thereby transferred His attribute from existing without a place to an attribute of existing in every place. So, according to you, the worshipped has changed and moved from no-place to every place. If he says: He existed in eternity in every place, just as He is now, then he has made places and things co-existent with Him in His eternity, and this is corrupt.

If he says: Is it permissible in your view that He who had no place in eternity moves to a place?

It is said to him: As for movement and change of state, there is no way to apply that to Him, because His existence in eternity does not require a place, and likewise His movement does not require a place. This is not like creation, because the existence of what exists requires "a place" for creatures, and their movement requires a place, and they become moving from one place to another, whereas Allah the Exalted is not like that. . . But we say: He "istawā" (rose over/settled) from no-place to a place, and we do not say "He moved," even though the meaning is the same in both. Just as we say "He has a throne" and do not say "He has a seat," and we say "He is the Wise" and do not say "He is the Intelligent," and we say "the Intimate friend (khalīl) of Abraham" and do not say "the close companion (ṣadīq) of Abraham," even though the meaning is the same. This is because we do not name Him, describe Him, or apply to Him except what He named Himself with, as has been stated before. We also do not reject what He described Himself with, for that would be rejecting the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾ (89:22).

His coming is not a motion, nor a removal, nor a transition, because these occur only when the one who comes is a body or a substance. Since it is established that He is not a body, nor a substance, nor an accident, it does not follow that His coming is a motion or a transfer. If you consider this by their saying, "his resurrection came upon so-and-so," "death came to him," "illness came to him," and similar expressions, for what is present and descends upon him is not a "coming" in the physical sense, it would become clear to you. And with Allah is protection and success.

If someone says: He cannot be "istawā" over a place except joined with a how (kayf), it is said to him: "istiwā'" may be obligatory while the "how" (taknīf, specifying a modality) is removed. Removing the "how" does not require removing the "istiwā'." If this were required, then the "how" would have been required in eternity, since He would not be existing in a place or joined to a modality. If he says that He existed without a place and was not joined to a modality, and we have understood and perceived by our senses that we have spirits in our bodies, and we do not know the modality of that, our ignorance of the modality of spirits does not require that we have no spirits. Likewise our ignorance of His modality on His throne does not require that He is not on His throne.

It has been narrated from Abu Razin al-'Uqaili who said:

"I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, where was our Lord, blessed and exalted, before He created the heavens and the earth?' He said, 'He was in 'amā', with nothing above Him, and nothing below Him, and He created the Throne upon the water.'"

Abu al-Qasim said: "'Amā'" (with a long mad) is a cloud, and "'amá" (with a short qaṣr) is darkness. The hadith has been narrated with both the long and the short forms. Whoever narrates it with the long form, its meaning according to him is: He was in a cloud, with what is below it and above it being air, and the pronoun refers to 'amā'. Whoever narrates it with the short form, its meaning according to him is: He was in a state of being "hidden" from His creation, because whoever is blinded from something is darkened concerning it.

Sunayd narrated with his chain from Mujahid, who said: "Between the Throne and the angels there are seventy veils, some of light and some of darkness." Sunayd also narrated with his chain from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The distance between the heaven and the earth is a five-hundred-year journey, and between each heaven and the next is a five-hundred-year journey, and between the seventh heaven and the Kursi is a five-hundred-year journey, and between the Kursi and the water is a five-hundred-year journey, and the Throne is upon the water, and Allah, glory be to Him, is above the Throne, and He knows your deeds."

Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, also said: "He is above the Throne, and nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him." Abu al-Qasim said: He means "above the Throne," because the Throne is the last of the created things, and there is nothing above it that is created, and Allah the Exalted is above the created things without modality, without contact. I know of no elevated (marfūʿ) hadith on this subject except the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umayra from al-Ahnaf from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at a cloud and said: "What do you call this?" They said: "The cloud (saḥāb)." He said: "And the rain-cloud (muzn)." They said: "And the rain-cloud." He said: "And the 'anān (cloud-layer)." They said: "And the 'anān." He said: "How far do you think there is between you and the sky?" They said: "We do not know." He said: "Between you and it is either one, or two, or seventy-three years, and the sky above it is likewise, and between them is the same distance," until he counted seven heavens. "Then above the seventh heaven is a sea, its top and bottom as far apart as between one heaven and another. Then above that are eight mountain goats, between their hooves and knees is as far as between one heaven and another. On their backs is the Throne, between its bottom and top is as far as between one heaven and another. Then Allah the Exalted is above that."

This is a hadith that is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ (good and sound), related by Abu Dawud.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 40, verses 38–39:**

He informed them that the world is something to be enjoyed for a time until something else, and that the Hereafter is the abode of permanence.

When you know that the pleasures of this world and its delights are a provision and a means to the pleasures of the Hereafter, and that for this reason the world and its pleasures were created, then every pleasure that helps one attain the pleasure of the Hereafter and leads to it is not blameworthy to partake of. Rather, it is praiseworthy in proportion to how far it leads to the pleasure of the Hereafter.

Once this is understood, the greatest bliss and pleasure of the Hereafter is: looking upon the Face of the Lord, glorified is His majesty, hearing His speech directly from Him, and nearness to Him. This is as established in the Sahih in the hadith of the vision: "By Allah, He has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking at Him." And in another hadith: "When He manifests Himself to them and they see Him, they forget whatever bliss they were in."

(Section)

Allah, glorified and exalted, created the creation only for the abode of permanence, and He placed all pleasure entirely within it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And therein is whatever the souls desire, and whatever the eyes delight in﴾. And He the Exalted said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah the Exalted says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, as a treasure, let alone what you have been shown of it."

That is, other than what you have been shown.

This is what the sincere adviser who was compassionate toward his people intended when he said: ﴿O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the path of right conduct. O my people, this worldly life is only a provision, and indeed the Hereafter is the abode of permanence﴾.

So He informed them that the world is a provision to be enjoyed for a time until something else, and that the Hereafter is the abode of permanence and the ultimate end.

Section: When it is known that the pleasures of this world and its delights are a provision and a means to the pleasures of the abode of the Hereafter, and that for this reason they were created, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "The world is a provision, and the best provision of the world is a righteous woman."

Then every pleasure that helps one attain the pleasures of the abode of the Hereafter is beloved and pleasing to the Lord, the Exalted. Its possessor enjoys it in two respects: from the aspect of his own delight and the comfort of his eye in it, and from the aspect of its leading him to the pleasure of his Lord and bringing him to a more complete pleasure than it. This is the pleasure a sensible person should strive to attain, not the pleasure that is followed by extreme pain and that forfeits for him the greatest pleasures. For this reason, the believer is rewarded for every permissible pleasure he enjoys when he intends by it to help himself and to reach the pleasure and bliss of the Hereafter. There is no comparison between the pleasure of one who has a wife or a beautiful slave-girl whom he loves, in whom his eye has found comfort, for when he is intimate with her and his heart, body, and soul delight in her company, he is rewarded for that pleasure, as opposed to the one who possesses forbidden pleasure, who is punished for his pleasure. As the Prophet ﷺ said:

"And in the intercourse of one of you there is a reward." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, does one of us fulfill his desire and still receive a reward for it?"

He said: "Do you not see that if he had placed it in the unlawful, he would bear a burden for it?" They said: "Yes."

He said: "Likewise, if he places it in the lawful, he will have a reward."

And know that this pleasure increases and grows in proportion to the servant's turning toward Allah, his sincerity in his deeds for Him, and his desire for the abode of the Hereafter. For desire and will, which are divided among many forms, are gathered for him in a single form, and the fear, worry, and grief that exist in forbidden pleasure are absent from his pleasure. So when a beautiful form befalls him along with this, and he is granted love for her and she is granted love for him, and the motives of his desire turn toward her, and his gaze is restricted from looking at anything else, and his soul from reaching for anything other than her, then there is no comparison between his pleasure and the pleasure of one with a forbidden form. This is the most excellent bliss that can be attained from this world. The Prophet ﷺ made it the third of three things through which one attains the good of this world and the Hereafter: a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and a beautiful wife who, when he looks at her, delights him, and when he is absent from her, she guards herself and his property.

So Allah is the One sought for help.

[Chapter: The Station of Tafwid (Entrusting)]

Among the stations of "You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help" (Q. 1:5) is the station of tafwid (complete entrusting).

The author of al-Manazil (Sahib al-Manazil) said:

It is subtler in its allusion and broader in meaning than tawakkul (reliance), for tawakkul comes after the means (sabab) has occurred, whereas tafwid comes before it occurs and after it. It is the very essence of istislam (submission). Tawakkul is a branch of it.

That is, the one who entrusts (mufawwid) disclaims might and power and hands the matter over to its Owner, without setting Him in his own place in his affairs. This is unlike tawakkul, for wakala (agency) requires that the agent stand in the place of the principal.

So tafwid is disavowal and departure from might and power, and the surrender of the entire matter to its Master.

It is said: Tawakkul is likewise, and what you have objected to in tawakkul applies equally to tafwid. For how can you entrust to its owner something you do not own at all? Can any one of the common subjects entrust sovereignty to the king of his time?

Thus the reason (illah) for objecting to tafwid is greater than for tawakkul. Indeed, if one said that tawakkul is above tafwid, more exalted and higher than it, he would be correct. For this reason the Qur'an is filled with it, both as a command and as a report about the special ones of God, the elite of His servants, that their condition is tawakkul. God commanded His Messenger to it in four places in His Book, and called him "the one who relies" (al-mutawakkil), as in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: "I read in the Torah the description of the Prophet ﷺ: Muhammad, the Messenger of God; I named him the one who relies, he is neither harsh nor coarse, nor clamorous in the markets."

He also reported that His messengers' condition was tawakkul, and by it they prevailed over their peoples. The Prophet ﷺ reported of the seventy thousand who enter Paradise without reckoning that they are the people of the station of tawakkul.

Tafwid does not come in the Qur'an except in what He related of the believer of Pharaoh's family, in his saying: "And I entrust my affair to God" (Q. 40:44).

God commanded His Messenger ﷺ to take Him as Agent (wakil), saying: "Lord of the East and the West, there is no god but Him, so take Him as Agent" (Q. 73:9).

This refutes the saying of some ignorant people that to make the Lord an agent is an audacity against the Originator, since tawakkul requires setting the agent in the place of the principal, and that is audacity itself.

He said: Were it not that God permitted that and recommended it, it would not be lawful for the servant to undertake it.

This is among the greatest ignorance, for taking Him as agent is the pure essence of servanthood and the pure essence of tawhid, when its bearer truly embodies it.

How excellent is the saying of the master of the people and the shaykh of the path, Sahl ibn Abdullah al-Tustari, when he said: "All knowledge is a door of worship, all worship is a door of scrupulousness (wara), all scrupulousness is a door of asceticism (zuhd), and all asceticism is a door of tawakkul."

So what we hold is that tawakkul is broader than tafwid, and higher and more exalted.

[Tafwid is more general than tawakkul]

His words: "for tawakkul comes after the means has occurred, whereas tafwid comes before it occurs and after it."

By "the means" he means acquisition (iktisab). The one who entrusts has entrusted his affair to God before acquiring and after it. The one who relies has stood by the means and relied upon God in it. So tafwid becomes broader.

It is said: Tawakkul may also be before the means, with it, and after it. One relies on God that He establish him in a means that conveys him to his goal. When he stands by it, he relies on God during its exercise. When he completes it, he relies on God for the attainment of its fruits. So he relies on God before it, with it, and after it.

On this basis, tawakkul is broader than tafwid, as stated.

His words: "It is the very essence of istislam; that is, tafwid is the very essence of complete submission to the Real, glorified is He, and one does not care whether what He decrees for him is good or otherwise. Whereas the one who relies relies on God in his affairs."

This is the aspect that the people noticed in belittling the station of tawakkul and elevating the station of tafwid above it.

Its answer is in two respects.

The first: the one who entrusts his affair to God does so only because he wills that He decree for him what is good for him in his livelihood and his hereafter, even if what is decreed for him is contrary to what he thinks good. He is content with it, because he knows it is good for him, even if the aspect of benefit in it is hidden from him. The condition of the one who relies is likewise, indeed higher than that of the one who entrusts, for with him is an act of the heart that is not with the one who entrusts. The one who relies is one who entrusts plus something more. The station of tawakkul is not upright except through tafwid, for when he entrusts his affair to Him, he leans with his whole heart upon Him after his tafwid.

An analogy: whoever entrusts his affair to a man and makes him its responsible party finds in himself, after entrusting, a special reliance, tranquility and calm toward the one entrusted, greater than what he had before entrusting. This is the reality of tawakkul.

The second: the most important of the one who relies' interests is the attainment of the pleasures and the loves of his Beloved. He relies on Him in attaining them for him. What interest is greater than this?

As for tafwid: it is the entrusting of the servant's livelihood needs and their causes to God, for he does not entrust to Him His loves. The one who relies relies on Him in His loves.

The delusion only entered from the perspective that the one who supposes assumes: that tawakkul is restricted to known provision, bodily strength and physical health. There is no doubt that this tawakkul is deficient in comparison with tawakkul in establishing the religion and calling to God.

[Degrees of tafwid]

He said: It has three degrees. The first: that he knows the servant possesses no capacity (istita'a) before his action. So he does not feel safe from deception (makr), does not despair of help, and does not rely on intention.

That is, he realizes that his capacity is in the hand of God, not in his own hand; He owns it, not him. If He does not give him capacity, he is incapable. He moves only by God, not by himself.

How can he feel safe from deception, when he is moved and not the mover? He is moved by the One whose motion is in His hand; if He wills, He holds him back and makes him sit with those who sit. As He said regarding those whom He denied this success: "But God disliked their setting out, so He held them back, and it was said: Sit with those who sit" (Q. 9:46).

This is God's deception (makr) against the servant: that He cuts off from him the sources of His success, leaves him between himself and his own self, does not stir his motives, and does not move him toward what pleases Him and what He loves. This is not an obligation upon God, so that He would be unjust in withholding it; exalted is God far above that. Rather it is pure bounty, which is praised when He gives it to whom He gives it, and praised when He withholds it from whom He withholds it. So to Him is praise for this and for that.

Whoever understands this has understood a great door of the secret of divine decree (qadar), and many problems become clear to him. He, glorified is He, does not will an act from Himself to be done to His servant, whereby what He loves and approves occurs from him, and then withholds from him the act of Himself in him, which is His success, because He dislikes it, and compels him to perform what provokes His wrath; rather He leaves him to his own self, his strength and his power, and forsakes him. This is the deception.

His words: "and does not despair of help," meaning when the one who moves him is the Lord, majestic in majesty, who is the most capable of the capable, who alone created and provided, and is the most merciful of the merciful. How could he despair of His help?

His words: "and does not rely on intention," that is, he does not depend upon his intention and resolve and trust in them. For his intention and resolve are in God's hand, not his, and they belong to God, not to him. So let his trust be in the One in whose hand they truly are, not in one upon whom they flow only as a judgment.

[Section: The second degree: witnessing compulsion]

He said: The second degree: witnessing compulsion (mu'ayanat al-idtirar). He sees no action as saving, no sin as destroying, and no cause as carrying.

That is, he witnesses his poverty, neediness and complete necessity toward God, such that in every atom of his inner and outer being he sees necessity and complete need toward God. So his salvation is only by God, not by his deed. As for his saying "and no sin as destroying": if he means that his destruction is by God and not by the cause of his sins, this is false, God forbid. If he means that God's grace, vastness, forgiveness and mercy, together with witnessing the intensity of his necessity and neediness toward Him, necessitate that he sees no sin as destroying, then his neediness, need and necessity prevent him from destruction by his sins, and indeed prevent him from plunging into destructive sins, since the possessor of this station does not persist in sins that would destroy him. If this is his state, then this is true, and it is among the witnessings of the people of gnosis (ma'rifa).

His words: "and no cause as carrying": that is, he witnesses that what carries him is the Real, exalted is He, not the means he undertakes. For he and them are carried by God alone.

[Section: The third degree: witnessing the sole possession of God over motion and rest]

He said: The third degree: witnessing the Real's sole ownership of motion and rest, of holding and extending, and knowing His disposal of separation (tafriqa) and gathering (jam').

This degree concerns witnessing God's attribute and affair, whereas the previous one concerned witnessing the servant's state and attribute. That is, he witnesses the motions and stillness of the world as issuing from the Real, exalted is He, in every moving and still thing. So he witnesses the connection of motion to His name al-Basit (the Extender) and the connection of stillness to His name al-Qabid (the Withholder), and thus witnesses His sole ownership of extension and withholding.

As for knowing His disposal of separation and gathering: it is that the witness knows the places of separation and gathering.

By separation is meant the consideration of the aspect of means and the attribution of actions to creatures.

By gathering is meant witnessing actions as attributed to their Originator, the Real, exalted is He.

Some use separation and gathering to mean a meaning beyond this witnessing, namely a state (hal). The state of separation is the scattering of the heart into the valleys and ravines of desires. The state of gathering is its collectedness upon the will of the Real alone. The first is the knowledge of separation and gathering; the second is their state. And God knows best.

(Fa'idah)
Al (āl, "family/household"): when used alone, it includes the person it is added to, as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Admit the family of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 46].
There is no doubt that it includes [Pharaoh himself] here, in his family.
And the words of the Exalted: ﴿And We certainly afflicted the family of Pharaoh with years [of drought]﴾ [al-A'raf: 130], and its like.
And the words of the Prophet ﷺ:
"O Allah, send blessings upon the family of Abi Awfa."
There is no doubt that Abi Awfa himself is included in that.
And his words: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim."
This is the wording in most narrations of al-Bukhari, and Ibrahim here is included in "his family." Perhaps this is what those who said "the family of a man" means the man himself intended.
But if a man is mentioned and then his family is mentioned, he is not included among them.
So there is a distinction between the unqualified and the qualified.
If you say, "Give to Zayd and the family of Zayd," Zayd is not included here in "his family."
But if you say, "Give to the family of Zayd," it covers Zayd and his family.
This has many parallels that we have mentioned in other places: that the indication of a word varies with being unqualified or qualified. For example, al-faqir and al-miskin are two categories when they are mentioned together, but one category when each is mentioned alone.
That is why they are two categories in zakat, and one category in expiations (kaffarat).
Likewise: al-iman and al-islam, al-birr and al-taqwa, al-fahsha' and al-munkar, al-fusuq and al-isyan.
Parallels to these are numerous, especially in the Qur'an.

(Section)
In the Musnad, from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said:
"We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the funeral of a man from the Ansar. We reached the grave, and it had not yet been lahd-dug. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat down and we sat around him as if birds were upon our heads. In his hand was a stick with which he was scratching the ground. He raised his head and said: 'Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave' — twice or three times —
Then he said: When the believing servant is turning away from the world and turning toward the Hereafter, there descend to him angels from the heaven with white faces, as if their faces were the sun, with them a shroud from the shrouds of the people of Paradise and spices from the spices of Paradise, until they sit at a distance of the eye's reach from him. Then the Angel of Death comes until he sits at his head and says: 'O soul at peace, come out to forgiveness from Allah and good pleasure.' So it comes out flowing like a drop flows from the mouth of a waterskin. He takes it, and when he has taken it they do not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye until they take it, and place it in that shroud and in those spices, and there comes out from it the finest fragrance of musk ever found on the face of the earth. They ascend with it, and they do not pass with it by any assembly of angels without them saying: 'What is this good spirit?' They say: 'The spirit of so-and-so, son of so-and-so,' using the best of his names by which he was called in the world. They ask for it to be opened for him, and it is opened for him. Those near to God in each heaven escort him to the heaven next to it, until he is brought to the seventh heaven. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Write the book of My servant in 'Illiyyin, and return him to the earth, for I created them from it, and in it I return them, and from it I bring them out once more.' He said: Then his spirit is returned to the earth, and two angels come to him and seat him, and they say to him: 'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'My Lord is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' They say to him: 'What is your religion?' He says: 'My religion is Islam.' They say to him: 'What is this man who was sent among you?' He says: 'He is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah.' They say to him: 'And what is your knowledge?' He says: 'I read the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so I believed in it and affirmed it.' Then a caller calls from the heaven: 'My servant has spoken the truth, so spread for him from Paradise, clothe him from Paradise, and open for him a door to Paradise.' He said: So there comes to him from its breeze and its fragrance, and his grave is widened for him as far as his eye can see. He said: And there comes to him a man of handsome face, fine clothes, and pleasant scent, and he says: 'Rejoice in that which will delight you; this is your day which you were promised.' He says to him: 'Who are you? Your face is the face that brings good.' He says: 'I am your righteous deed.' He says: 'My Lord, establish the Hour, my Lord, establish the Hour, so that I may return to my family and my wealth.'
He said: And when the disbelieving servant is turning away from the world and turning toward the Hereafter, there descend to him angels from the heaven, black of face, with them coarse garments, and they sit at a distance of the eye's reach from him. Then the Angel of Death comes until he sits at his head and says: 'O wicked soul, come out to the wrath and anger of Allah.' He said: So it scatters through his body, and he extracts it as an iron skewer is pulled from wet wool. He takes it, and when he has taken it they do not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye, until they place it in those coarse garments, and there comes out from it the foulest stench of a carcass ever found on the face of the earth. They ascend with it, and they do not pass with it by any assembly of angels without them saying: 'What is this wicked spirit?' They say: 'The spirit of so-and-so, son of so-and-so,' using the worst of his names by which he was called in the world. It is requested to be opened, but it is not opened for him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾ [al-A'raf: 40].
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Write his book in Sijjin, in the lowest earth,' so his spirit is cast down violently. Then he recited: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds snatched him, or the wind threw him into a far place﴾ [al-Hajj: 31].
Then his spirit is returned into his body, and two angels come to him and seat him, and they say to him: 'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'Hah hah, I do not know.' They say to him: 'What is your religion?' He says: 'Hah hah, I do not know.' They say to him: 'What is this man who was sent among you?'
He says: 'Hah hah, I do not know.' Then a caller calls from the heaven: 'My servant has lied, so spread for him from the Fire, and open for him a door to the Fire.' So there comes to him from its heat and its scorching wind, and his grave is constricted upon him until his ribs interlock. And there comes to him a man of ugly face, ugly clothes, and foul smell, and he says: 'Be dismayed by that which will harm you; this is your day which you were promised.' He says: 'And who are you? Your face is the face that brings evil.' He says: 'I am your wicked deed.' He says: 'My Lord, do not establish the Hour.'"
In another wording of Ahmad also: "Then there is appointed for him a blind, deaf, mute one, with a mace in his hand, which if he struck a mountain with it, it would become dust. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, restores him as he was, and he strikes him another blow, and he cries out a cry that everything hears except the two worlds (jinn and humans)." Al-Bara' said: "Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and from the bedding of the Fire is spread out for him."
Also in the Musnad, from him, he said:
"While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he saw a group of people and said: 'What have these gathered for?' It was said: 'Over a grave they are digging.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was alarmed, and hastened ahead of his companions until he reached the grave, and he knelt on his knees. I went before him to see what he would do, and he wept until the earth was wet from his tears. Then he turned to us and said: 'O my brothers, for a day like this, prepare.'"
Also in the Musnad, from the hadith of Buraydah, who said:
"The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us one day and called out three times: 'O people, do you know what my example and your example is?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'My example and your example is that of a people who feared an enemy coming upon them, so they sent a man to watch for them. He saw the enemy, and came hastening to warn them, but he feared the enemy would overtake him before he warned his people, so he waved his garment: O people, you have been come upon! O people, you have been come upon! Three times.'"
Also in the Musnad, from the hadith of Abu Dhar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I see what you do not see, and I hear what you do not hear. The heaven creaks, and it has the right to creak; there is no place the size of four fingers in it except that there is an angel prostrating upon it. If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, and you would not enjoy women on beds, and you would go out to the high ground crying out to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."
Abu Dhar said: "By Allah, I wish I were a tree that is cut down."
Also in the Musnad, from the hadith of Hudhayfah, who said:
"We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at a funeral, and when we reached the grave he sat on his shins, and began to look steadily into it. Then he said: 'The believer is pressed in it with a pressing that makes his ribs shift, and the disbeliever is filled with fire, and the ribs are the veins of the two testicles.'"
Also in the Musnad, from the hadith of Jabir, who said:
"We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh when he died. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had prayed over him, and he was placed in his grave and leveled over him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ glorified Allah, and we glorified Allah for a long time. Then he exclaimed 'Allahu akbar,' and we exclaimed it too. It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why did you glorify, then exclaim takbir?' He said: 'His grave had become constricted upon this righteous servant until Allah relieved him of it.'"
In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the funeral is placed and men carry it on their necks, if it is righteous it says: 'Send me forward, send me forward!' and if it is not righteous it says: 'Woe to it! Where are you taking it?' Everything hears its voice except humankind, and if a human heard it, he would faint."
In the Musnad of Ahmad, from the hadith of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"On the Day of Resurrection the sun will draw near to the distance of a mile, and its heat will be increased so-and-so much; the heads will boil as pots boil. They will sweat in it according to their sins: some of them will reach to their ankles, some to their shins, some to their waists, and some will be bridled by the sweat."
And in it, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said:
"How can I be at ease when the holder of the horn has taken the horn into his mouth, and bowed his forehead, listening for when he will be commanded to blow?"
His companions said: "What should we say?" He said: "Say: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In Allah we have put our trust.'"
Also in the Musnad, from Ibn 'Umar, raised to the Prophet:
"Whoever considers himself great, or swaggers in his walk, will meet Allah while He is angry with him."
In the Two Sahihs, from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Those who make images will be punished on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to them: 'Give life to what you have created.'"
In the two of them also, from him, from the Prophet ﷺ:
"When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him in the morning and the evening: if he is among the people of Paradise, then [it is shown as] of the people of Paradise; and if he is among the people of the Fire, then of the people of the Fire. It is said: 'This is your seat, until Allah raises you on the Day of Resurrection.'"
In the two of them also, from him, from the Prophet ﷺ:
"When the people of Paradise are in Paradise and the people of the Fire are in the Fire, Death will be brought and stood between Paradise and the Fire, then slaughtered. Then a caller calls: 'O people of Paradise, eternity, no death! O people of the Fire, eternity, no death!' So the people of Paradise increase in joy upon their joy, and the people of the Fire increase in grief upon their grief."

[Section: The punishment of the grave and the relation of the body and spirit to it]
This becomes clear by answering the question, namely the questioner's saying: Is the punishment of the grave upon the soul and the body, or upon the soul without the body, or upon the body without the soul? And does the body share with the soul in bliss and punishment or not?
The Shaykh al-Islam was asked about this question, and we mention the wording of his answer. He said: Rather, the punishment and bliss are upon both the soul and the body together, by the consensus of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah. The soul is blessed and punished separately from the body, and blessed and punished connected to the body, with the body connected to it. So the bliss and punishment in this state are upon both together, just as they are upon the spirit separated from the body. As for whether bliss and punishment are upon the body without the spirit, there are two well-known opinions among the people of hadith and Sunnah and the people of kalam. In the matter there are odd sayings that are not from the sayings of Ahl al-Sunnah and hadith: the saying of those who say that bliss and punishment occur only upon spirits, and that the body is neither blessed nor punished. This is said by the philosophers who deny the return of bodies, and they are unbelievers by the consensus of the Muslims. And many of the people of kalam, among the Mu'tazilah and others, who affirm the return of bodies, say that this does not occur in the barzakh, but only at rising from the graves; yet these deny the punishment of the body in the barzakh alone, and say: the spirits are the ones blessed or punished in the barzakh, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, both the spirit and the body are punished together.
This saying was held by groups of Muslims from among the people of kalam, hadith and others, and it is the choice of Ibn Hazm and Ibn Murrah. This saying is not among the three odd sayings; rather it is added to the saying of the one who affirms the punishment of the grave, acknowledges the Resurrection, and affirms the return of bodies and spirits. But these have three opinions regarding the punishment of the grave:
The first: that it is upon the spirit only.
The second: that it is upon it and upon the body through its means.

The third view is that the punishment falls on the body alone. This may be combined with the second view, namely that of those who affirm the punishment of the grave and make the soul to be life itself. The aberrant views are the view of those who deny the punishment of bodies absolutely, and the view of those who deny the punishment of souls absolutely. If the aberrant views are counted as three, then the second aberrant view is that of those who say that the soul on its own neither experiences bliss nor punishment, and that the soul is merely life. This is said by groups among the theologians (ahl al-kalam), including the Mu'tazilah and the Ash'arites such as al-Qadi Abu Bakr and others, and they deny that the soul remains after separation from the body. This is a false view, and even its own adherents were opposed to it, including Abu al-Ma'ali al-Juwayni and others. Indeed, it has been established by the Book, the Sunnah and the consensus of the Community (ijma') that the soul remains after separation from the body and that it is either blissful or punished. The divine philosophers (al-falasifah al-ilahiyyun) also affirm this.

However, they deny the resurrection of bodies, whereas these groups affirm the resurrection of bodies but deny the resurrection of souls and their bliss and punishment apart from bodies. Both views are error and misguidance, but the view of the philosophers is further removed from the views of the people of Islam, even though it is agreed upon by those who believe themselves to adhere to the religion of Islam, indeed by those who think themselves to be among the people of gnosis (ma'rifah), Sufism, verification (tahqiq) and theology (kalam).

The third aberrant view is the view of those who say: the barzakh (intermediate state) contains neither bliss nor punishment; rather, these only occur after the Great Hour arrives. This is the view of the Mu'tazilah and their like who deny the punishment of the grave and its bliss, on the basis that the soul does not remain after separation from the body and that the body neither experiences bliss nor punishment. All of these groups are astray regarding the matter of the barzakh, but they are better than the philosophers, for they affirm the Great Resurrection.

[Section: The position of the early generations regarding the punishment of the dead]

Having understood these false views, know that the position of the early generations of the Community (salaf al-ummah) and its imams is that when the dead person dies, he is in bliss or in punishment, and that this occurs to his soul and to his body. The soul remains after separation from the body, blissful or punished, and it is sometimes connected to the body, and bliss or punishment is experienced by the body together with it. Then, when the Great Day of Resurrection comes, the souls are returned to the bodies, and they rise from their graves to the Lord of the worlds. The resurrection of bodies is agreed upon among the Muslims, the Jews and the Christians. We affirm what we have mentioned.

As for the hadiths on the punishment of the grave and the matter of Munkar and Nakir, they are numerous and widely transmitted (mutawatir) from the Prophet (ﷺ), as in the Two Sahihs from Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by two graves and said: "Indeed, they are being punished, and they are not being punished for a great matter. As for one of them, he did not guard himself against urine; and as for the other, he used to go about with tale-bearing." Then he asked for a fresh palm frond, split it in two, and said: "Perhaps it will lighten their punishment as long as they have not dried out."

(In Sahih Muslim) from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: While the Prophet (ﷺ) was in an orchard belonging to the Banu al-Najjar, riding on his mule, and we were with him, the mule shied and nearly threw him off. Then there were six or five or four graves. He said: "Who knows the people of these graves?" A man said: "I do." He said: "When did these die?" He said: "They died in polytheism." He said: "Indeed, this community is tested in its graves. Were it not that you would not bury one another, I would supplicate Allah that He let you hear the punishment of the grave that I hear." Then he turned his face toward us and said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the Fire." They said: "We seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the Fire." He said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave." They said: "We seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave." He said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the trials, what is apparent of them and what is hidden." They said: "We seek refuge with Allah from the trials, what is apparent of them and what is hidden." He said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the trial of the Dajjal." They said: "We seek refuge with Allah from the trial of the Dajjal."

(In Sahih Muslim) and all the Sunan from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When one of you finishes the final tashahhud, let him seek refuge with Allah from four things: from the punishment of Jahannam, from the punishment of the grave, from the trial of life and death, and from the trial of the Messiah al-Dajjal."

(In Sahih Muslim) also and others, from Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to teach them this supplication as he taught them a surah of the Qur'an: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Jahannam, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of life and death, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the Messiah al-Dajjal."

(In the Two Sahihs) from Abu Ayyub, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) went out after the sun had set, and he heard a sound and said: "Jews are being punished in their graves."

(In the Two Sahihs) from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: An old woman from the old women of the Jews of Madinah came to me and said: "Indeed the people of the graves are punished in their graves." She said: I denied her and did not believe her. She said: Then I went out, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, an old woman from the old women of the Jews of Madinah came in and claimed that the people of the graves are punished in their graves!" He said: "She spoke the truth; indeed they are punished with a punishment that all the animals hear." She said: I never saw him afterward in prayer without seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave.

(In Sahih Ibn Hibban) from Umm Mubashshir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me while I was in an orchard of the orchards of the Banu al-Najjar, in which there were graves of some of them, and he was saying: "Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there punishment in the grave?" He said: "Indeed they are punished in their graves with a punishment that the animals hear."

(Some scholars said:) For this reason, people take their animals, when they become ill with a wasting disease (maghl), to the graves of the Jews, Christians and hypocrites such as the Isma'iliyyah, the Nusayriyyah and the Qaramitah of the Banu 'Ubayd and others, who are in the land of Egypt and Syria. Horsemen intentionally go to their graves for this purpose, just as they go to the graves of the Jews and Christians. He said: When the horses hear the punishment of the grave, that produces in them fear and heat which removes the wasting disease.

(And) 'Abd al-Haqq al-Ishbili said: The jurist Abu al-Hakam ibn Barjan, who was among the people of knowledge and action, related to me that they buried a dead man in their village in the outskirts of Seville. When they had finished burying him, they sat to one side talking, and a beast was grazing near them. Suddenly the beast came rushing toward the grave, placed its ear upon it as if listening, then fled, then returned to the grave and placed its ear upon it as if listening, then fled again. It kept doing this time after time.

Abu al-Hakam said: I remembered the punishment of the grave and the words of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed they are punished with a punishment that the animals hear."

This story was related to us while we were listening to the Sahih of Muslim, when the reader reached the Prophet's words (ﷺ): "Indeed they are punished with a punishment that the animals hear."

This hearing occurs on the voices of the punished. Hannad ibn al-Sarri said in the book al-Zuhd: Waki' related to us from al-A'mash from Shaqiq from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said:
A Jewish woman came in upon me and mentioned the punishment of the grave, and I denied her. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon me and I mentioned that to him, and he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed they are punished in their graves until the animals hear their voices."

(I say:) The hadiths on the matter of the grave are numerous, as in the Two Sahihs and the Sunan, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the believer is questioned in his grave and testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, that is the meaning of Allah's words: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾."

In another wording: It was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave. It is said to him: Who is your Lord? He says: Allah is my Lord and Muhammad is my prophet. That is the meaning of Allah's words: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾.

The hadith has been related by the people of the Sunan and the Musnads at length, as has already been mentioned.

In this hadith it is clearly stated that the soul is returned to the body and that its ribs are interlocked, and this is clear evidence that the punishment falls on the soul and body together.

Similar to the hadith of al-Bara' is the hadith of Abu Hurayrah concerning the seizing of the soul, the questioning, the bliss and the punishment, in the Musnad and the Sahih of Abu Hatim, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the dead person, when placed in his grave, hears the sound of their sandals as they turn away from him. If he was a believer, prayer is at his head, fasting is at his right, zakah is at his left, and the doing of good deeds—charity, kinship ties, kindness and benevolence—is at his feet. He is approached from the direction of his head, and prayer says: 'There is no entry from my side.' Then he is approached from his right, and fasting says: 'There is no entry from my side.' Then he is approached from his left, and zakah says: 'There is no entry from my side.' Then he is approached from the direction of his feet, and the doing of good deeds—charity, kinship, kindness and benevolence—says: 'There is no entry from my side.' Then it is said to him: 'Sit up.' He sits up, and the sun has been depicted for him as it is about to set. It is said to him: 'This man who was among you, what do you say about him and what do you testify concerning him?' He says: 'Let me pray.' They say: 'You will pray. Tell us what we ask you. What do you say about this man who was among you, and what do you testify concerning him?' He says: 'Muhammad? I testify that he is the Messenger of Allah, who brought the truth from Allah.' It is said to him: 'Upon that you lived, upon that you died, and upon that you will be resurrected, if Allah wills.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This is your seat and what Allah has prepared for you in it.' He increases in joy and delight. Then his grave is widened for him seventy cubits, and it is illuminated for him, and the body is returned to what it was created from, and his soul is made one of the good souls, and it is a bird suspended in a tree of Paradise." He said: "That is the meaning of Allah's words: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾." He mentioned the opposite of that concerning the disbeliever, until he said: "Then the grave is constricted for him until his ribs are interlocked, and that is the straitened life of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, for him is a straitened life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾."

(In the Two Sahihs) from the hadith of Qatadah, from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the dead person, when placed in his grave and his companions turn away from him, he hears the sound of their sandals. Two angels come to him and seat him and say to him: 'What did you used to say about this man, Muhammad?' As for the believer, he says: 'I testify that he is the servant of Allah and His Messenger.' He says: 'Look at your seat in the Fire; Allah has replaced it for you with a seat in Paradise.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He sees them both." Qatadah said: It has been related to us that his grave is widened seventy cubits and it is filled with greenery until the Day they are resurrected.

He then returned to the hadith of Anas, who said: As for the disbeliever and the hypocrite, they say to him: "What did you used to say about this man?" He says: "I do not know; I used to say what the people said." They say: "You did not know and you did not recite." Then he is struck between his ears with a hammer of iron, and he cries out a cry that everything near him hears except the two jinn and humans.

(In Sahih Abi Hatim) from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you is buried, or a person is buried, two angels come to him, black and blue, called Munkar and Nakir. They say to him: 'What did you used to say about this man, Muhammad (ﷺ)?' He will say what he used to say. If he was a believer, he says: 'He is the servant of Allah and His Messenger; I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' They say to him: 'We knew that you would say that.' Then his grave is widened for him seventy cubits by seventy cubits, and it is illuminated for him, and it is said to him: 'Sleep.' He says: 'Let me return to my family and my property and inform them.' They say: 'Sleep like the sleep of a bride whom none wakes except the dearest of her family to her, until Allah raises him from that resting place.' If he was a hypocrite, he says: 'I do not know; I used to hear the people say something and I used to say it.' They say to him: 'We knew that you would say that.' Then it is said to the earth: 'Close in upon him,' and it closes in upon him until his ribs are interlocked, and he remains punished until Allah raises him from that resting place." This is explicit that the body is punished.

(And from Abu Hurayrah) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the believer is at the point of death, the angels come to him with a white silk cloth and say: 'Come out, O pure soul, pleased and well-pleasing, to comfort and sweet scent and a Lord not angry.' It comes out like the finest scent of musk, until one of them hands it to another until they bring it to the gate of heaven. They say: 'How fine is this scent that has come to you from the earth!' They bring it to the souls of the believers, and they are more joyful at it than one of you is at an absent person who arrives to him. They ask it: 'What did so-and-so do?' It says: 'Leave him to rest, for he was in the distress of the world.' When it says: 'He has come to you,' they say: 'He has been taken to his mother, the Abyss.' As for the disbeliever, when he is at the point of death, the angels of punishment come to him with a coarse garment and say: 'Come out, O soul displeased with, to the punishment of Allah,' and it comes out like the foulest stench of a carcass, until they bring it to the gate of the earth. They say: 'How foul is this soul,' until they bring it to the souls of the disbelievers." Related by al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar and Muslim in abridged form.

(Abu Hatim also related it in his Sahih) and said: "When death attends the believer, the angels of mercy attend him; when he is taken, his soul is placed in a white silk cloth, and it is taken up to the gate of heaven. They say: 'We have found no scent better than this.' It is said: 'What did so-and-so do? What did so-and-so do?' It is said: 'Leave him to rest, for he was in the distress of the world.' As for the disbeliever, when his soul is taken, it is taken down to the earth. The guardians of the earth say: 'We have found no scent fouler than this,' and it is carried down to the lowest earth."

(And it was related) by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "This one, for whom the Throne shook and the gates of heaven were opened and seventy thousand angels bore witness, was squeezed with a squeeze and then released." Al-Nasa'i said: He means Sa'd ibn Mu'adh.

(And it was related) from the hadith of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The grave has a squeeze; if anyone were to escape it, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh would have escaped it," related from the hadith of Shu'bah.

Hannad ibn al-Sarri said: Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl related to us from his father from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: "No one is spared the squeeze of the grave, not even Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, one of whose handkerchiefs is better than the world and what is in it."

He also said: 'Abdah from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar related to us from Nafi', who said: It has reached me that seventy thousand angels attended the funeral of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, who had never before descended to the earth. It has reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Your companion was squeezed in the grave with a squeeze."

'Ali ibn Ma'bad said: 'Ubayd Allah related to us from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Jabir, from Nafi', who said: We came to Safiyyah bint Abi 'Ubayd, the wife of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, and she was frightened. We asked her: "What is the matter with you?" She said: "I came from the presence of some of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)," and she said: "He related to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If anyone were to be spared the punishment of the grave, I would have thought Sa'd ibn Mu'adh would be spared it; he was squeezed in it with a squeeze.'"

(And) Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us from 'Ala' ibn al-Musayyib from Mu'awiyah al-'Absi from Zadhan ibn 'Amr, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) buried his daughter, he sat by the grave, and his face became troubled, then it cleared. His companions said to him: "We saw your face change a moment ago, then it cleared." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I remembered my daughter and her weakness and the punishment of the grave, so I supplicated Allah and He relieved her. By Allah, she was squeezed with a squeeze that was heard between the two horizons."

Shu'ayb related to us from Ibn Dinar from Ibrahim al-Ghanawi from a man who said: I was with 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) when a funeral of a small child passed, and she wept. I said to her: "What makes you weep, O Mother of the Believers?" She said: "I wept for this child out of compassion for him from the squeeze of the grave."

It is well known that all of this occurs through the medium of the soul.

[Section: Belief in the punishment of the grave]

This, just as it is the requirement of the authentic Sunnah, is agreed upon among the people of the Sunnah. al-Marwazi said: Abu 'Abd Allah said: "The punishment of the grave is true; none denies it except a misguided misleader." Hanbal said:

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 40, verse 45–46 (part 3 of 5):

I said to Abu ʿAbd Allah (Ahmad ibn Hanbal) concerning the punishment of the grave, and he said: "These are sound traditions (ahadith sihah). We believe in them and affirm them. Whenever a sound chain (isnad jayyid) comes from the Prophet ﷺ, we affirm it. If we do not affirm what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought, and we reject it and push it away, we would be rejecting the command of Allah. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾."

I said to him: "And is the punishment of the grave true?" He said: "It is true; they are punished in the grave."

He said: "I heard Abu ʿAbd Allah say: We believe in the punishment of the grave, in Munkar and Nakir, and that the servant is questioned in his grave, so that Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, in the grave."

(And) Ahmad ibn al-Qasim said: I said: "O Abu ʿAbd Allah, do you affirm Munkar and Nakir, and what is related about the punishment of the grave?" He said: "Subhan Allah, yes, we affirm that and say it." I said: "Does this wording say 'Munkar and Nakir' like this, or does it say 'two angels'?" He said: "Munkar and Nakir." I said: "They say there is no mention of Munkar and Nakir in a hadith." He said: "It is like this," meaning that they are Munkar and Nakir.

As for the views of the people of innovation (ahl al-bidʿah) and misguidance: Abu al-Hudhayl and al-Marisi said: whoever departs from the description of faith, he is punished between the two blasts, and the questioning in the grave occurs only at that time.

Al-Jubba'i and his son al-Balkhi affirmed the punishment of the grave, but they denied it for the believers, and affirmed it for those who are eternally abiding (in the Fire) among the disbelievers and the grave-sinners, according to their principles.

(And) many of the Mu'tazilah said: it is not permissible to name Allah's angels Munkar and Nakir; rather, "munkar" is what appears of his faltering when he is questioned, and "nakir" is the two angels' rebuke of him.

Al-Salihi said, and Salih (ibn ʿAbd al-Quddus?) held that the punishment of the grave applies to the believer without the return of the souls to the bodies, and that the dead may feel pain, perceive and know without a soul; this is the view of a group of the Karramiyyah.

(And) some of the Mu'tazilah said: Allah the Exalted punishes the dead in their graves and inflicts pains upon them while they are unaware; when they are resurrected, He brings those pains into being and they feel them. They said: the state of those punished among the dead is like that of the drunkard and the one who has fainted: if they are struck they do not feel the blows, but when their reason returns they feel the pain of the striking.

Some of them, such as Dirar ibn ʿAmr and Yahya ibn Kamil, and it is the view of al-Muribi, altogether denied the punishment of the grave. These are the views of the people of disgrace and misguidance.

[Section: Refutation of those who deny the punishment of the grave]

This is the question of the questioner: what is our answer to the heretics (malahidah) and the zindiqs who deny the punishment of the grave, its spaciousness and its constriction, and that it is a pit of the pits of the Fire or a garden of the gardens of Paradise, and that the deceased neither sits nor rises in it.

They say: "We uncover the grave and find no angels, blind and deaf, striking the dead with hammers of iron, nor do we find there serpents, snakes, or fires blazing. If we uncovered its condition at any moment we would find it unchanged; and if we placed mercury on its eyes and mustard on its chest, we would find it in its state. How can it be widened as far as the eye sees, or constricted, when we find it in its condition and find its dimensions just as we dug them, neither more nor less? How can that narrow niche contain him, together with the angels and the form that comforts him or frightens him?" Their brethren from the people of innovation and misguidance said, and every hadith that contradicts what is rationally and sensorily established is to be judged erroneous, they said: "We see the crucified man on a wooden cross for a long period, and he is not questioned, does not answer, does not move, and his body does not burn with fire. And the one whom beasts have devoured, and birds have torn apart, and whose parts are scattered in the bellies of beasts, the crops of birds, the stomachs of fish, and the paths of winds, how will his parts be questioned while they are scattered? How can the questioning of the two angels be imagined for one of this description? How can the grave become a garden of the gardens of Paradise or a pit of the pits of the Fire on this basis? How can it constrict upon him until his ribs interlock? We will mention matters by which the answer may be known.

The first matter: it should be known that the Messengers, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon them, did not report anything that the intellects deem impossible and judge to be impossible. Rather, their reports are of two kinds:

One: what the intellects and natural dispositions (fitar) bear witness to.

Second: what the intellects do not grasp by themselves, such as the unseen matters they reported concerning the details of the barzakh (intermediate realm) and the Last Day, and the details of reward and punishment. Their report is not impossible for the intellects at all. Every report that is thought to be rejected by reason falls under one of two matters: either the report is a lie attributed to them, or that reason is corrupt, and it is an imaginary doubt which its holder thinks is clear, manifest reason. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. And He the Exalted said: ﴿So is one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾

And He the Exalted said: ﴿And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been sent down to you, and among the factions are those who deny part of it﴾.

Souls do not rejoice in the impossible. And He the Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, there has come to you an admonition from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers. Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, so in that let them rejoice"﴾.

The impossible does not heal, nor is guidance or mercy attained through it, nor does one rejoice in it.

This is the matter of one in whose heart goodness has not settled and in whom firmness in Islam has not taken root, and the best of his conditions is bewilderment and doubt.

The second matter: that one understands from the Messenger ﷺ his intended meaning without exaggeration or diminution, so that his words are not burdened with what they cannot bear, nor reduced below what he intended of guidance and clarification.

By neglecting this and turning away from it there results from misguidance and deviation from the right what no one knows except Allah. Indeed, misunderstanding of Allah and His Messenger is the root of every innovation and misguidance that has arisen in Islam; indeed, it is the root of every error in the fundamentals and the subsidiaries. This is especially so when bad intention is added to it, so that misunderstanding occurs in some matters from a leader whose intention is good, and bad intention from a follower, to the affliction of the religion and its people. And Allah is the One sought for help.

Did anything cause the Qadariyyah, the Murji'ah, the Kharijites, the Mu'tazilah, the Jahmiyyah and all the other sects of innovation to fall except misunderstanding of Allah and His Messenger, until the religion in the hands of most people became the consequence of these understandings? And what the Companions and those who followed them understood from Allah and His Messenger is abandoned, unregarded, and these people do not lift their heads to it at all. Because the examples of this principle are so many, we have left them out; for if we mentioned them they would exceed ten thousand, to the extent that you pass through a book from its beginning to its end and do not find its author understanding Allah and His Messenger and their intent as he should in a single place.

This is known only by one who knows what people have and presents it to what the Messenger brought. As for one who reverses the matter, presenting what the Messenger brought to what he believes, adopts, and follows blindly from one whose opinion he thinks well of, speech is of no use with him, so leave him, and what he has chosen for himself, upon him is what he has taken on. And praise be to Allah who has spared you from what He has tested him with.

The third matter: Allah the Exalted made the abodes three: the abode of this world, the abode of the barzakh, and the abode of permanence (dar al-qarar). He made for each abode rulings specific to it. He composed this human being of body and soul (nafs). He made the rulings of the abode of this world apply to the bodies and souls as a consequence of it, and for this reason He made His legal rulings dependent upon what appears of the movements of the tongue and the limbs, even if souls conceal the opposite. He made the rulings of the barzakh apply to souls and bodies as a consequence of it. Just as souls followed bodies in the rulings of this world, feeling their pain and enjoying their ease, and it was they who engaged the causes of bliss and punishment, so bodies follow souls in their bliss and punishment. Then the souls are those which engage bliss and punishment. So here the bodies are apparent and the souls hidden; and in the grave the bodies are hidden in their graves, and the souls there are apparent. The rulings of the barzakh apply to souls, and they flow into their bodies as bliss or punishment, just as the rulings of this world apply to bodies, and they flow into their souls as bliss or punishment. So comprehend this station fully and know it as it should be, and it will remove from you every problem that is raised against you from within and without.

Allah, in His kindness, mercy and guidance, has shown us from this a model in this world: the state of the sleeper. What he is blessed with or punished with in his sleep applies to his soul essentially, and the body follows it. It may grow strong until it affects the body in a visible way: the sleeper sees that he was struck, and in the morning the trace of the blow is on his body; he sees that he ate or drank, and he wakes up finding the trace of food and drink in his mouth, and hunger and thirst depart from him.

More wondrous than that: you see the sleeper rise in his sleep and strike, seize and defend himself as if he were awake, while he is asleep and has no awareness of any of that. That is because when the ruling applies to the soul, it seeks help from the body from outside it; if it entered it, he would awaken and perceive. So if the soul is pained and blessed, and that reaches its body by way of following, then likewise in the barzakh, indeed greater, for the soul's detachment there is more complete and stronger, while it remains attached to its body, not severed from it entirely. When the day of the resurrection of bodies comes and people rise from their graves, the ruling, bliss and punishment become in both souls and bodies apparent and manifest.

When you give this station its due, it becomes clear to you that what the Messenger reported of the punishment of the grave, its bliss, its constriction and spaciousness, its squeezing, and that it is a pit of the pits of the Fire or a garden of the gardens of Paradise, is consistent with reason, and that it is true without doubt; and that whoever finds this difficult, it is from his misunderstanding and little knowledge, coming as it has been said:

"How many a critic of a sound saying, whose affliction is from a sick understanding."

More wondrous than that: you find a sleeper in one bed, whose soul is in bliss and who wakes with the trace of bliss on his body, and another whose soul is in punishment and who wakes with the trace of punishment on his body, and neither has knowledge of what the other has. So the matter of the barzakh is more wondrous than that.

The fourth matter: Allah the Exalted made the matter of the Hereafter and what is connected to it unseen, and veiled it from the perception of the responsible in this abode, and that is from the perfection of His wisdom, and so that the believers in the unseen may be distinguished from others. The first of that: the angels descend upon the dying person and sit near him, and he sees them directly and they converse in his presence, and with them are the shrouds and the hanut (perfume), either from Paradise or from the Fire, and they say amen to the supplications of those present for good and for evil. They may greet the dying person, and he returns the greeting sometimes with a word, sometimes with his gesture, and sometimes with his heart, when he cannot speak or gesture.

Some of the dying have been heard to say: "Welcome and hello and marhaban to these faces."

My shaykh reported to me about a certain dying person, and I do not know whether I witnessed it and am reporting it, that he was heard saying: "Peace upon you here, so sit down"; "Peace upon you here, so sit down."

The account of al-Nassaj, may Allah have mercy on him, is well known, when at death he said: "Be patient, may Allah grant you well-being, for what you have been commanded does not perish, and what you have been commanded does perish." Then he called for water, performed ablution, prayed, then said: "Proceed to what you were commanded," and died.

[Section: The nature of the fire and greenery in the grave]

The fifth and sixth matters: the fire that is in the grave and the greenery are not of the fire of this world nor of the plants of this world, so that whoever witnesses the fire and greenery of this world sees them; rather they are of the fire of the Hereafter and its greenery, and it is more severe than the fire of this world, so the people of this world do not perceive it. For Allah the Exalted heats that earth and the stones which are upon him and beneath him until it is more intensely hot than the embers of this world; and if the people of this world touched it they would not perceive that. Indeed, more wondrous than this: two men may be buried side by side, one in a pit of the pits of the Fire whose heat does not reach his neighbour, and the other in a garden of the gardens of Paradise whose spirit and bliss do not reach his neighbour.

The power of the Lord, exalted is He, is wider and more wondrous than that, and Allah has shown us in this abode signs of His power far more wondrous than that; but souls are inclined to deny what they do not comprehend, except those whom Allah grants success and protects.

For the disbeliever two slabs of fire are spread out, and his grave blazes with them as an oven blazes. When Allah the Exalted wills to let some of His servants perceive that, He lets him perceive it and hides it from others; for if all the servants perceived it, the word of obligation and faith in the unseen would vanish, and people would not bury one another, as in the two Sahihs from him ﷺ: "Were it not that you would stop burying one another, I would supplicate Allah to make you hear the punishment of the grave as I hear it."

And since this wisdom is negated concerning animals, they hear that and perceive it, as happened to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when a camel reached him and nearly threw him off when he passed by someone being punished in his grave.

(And) my companion Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Ruzayz al-Harrani related to me that he went out from his house after the afternoon prayer at Amid to a garden. He said: "When it was before sunset, I passed among the graves, and there was a grave among them that was a blazing ember like a glass jar, with the dead person in its midst. I began rubbing my eyes and saying: 'Am I asleep or awake?' Then I turned to the city wall and said: 'By Allah, I am not asleep.' Then I went to my family, bewildered, and they brought me food but I could not eat. Then I entered the town and asked about the owner of the grave, and he was a tax collector who had died that day."

The seeing of this fire in the grave is like the seeing of angels, and the jinn sometimes occur to whoever Allah wills to show that.

(And) Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned in the book "al-Qubur" from al-Shaʿbi that he mentioned a man who said to the Prophet ﷺ: "I passed by Badr and saw a man emerging from the earth, and a man struck him with a maqma'ah (iron rod) until he disappeared into the earth, then he emerged and it was done again." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That is Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, who is punished until the Day of Resurrection."

(And) he mentioned from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah from ʿAmr ibn Dinar from Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah from his father, who said: "While I was travelling between Makkah and Madinah on a riding camel, with my ihdar (a bag) tied behind me, I passed by a cemetery, and there was a man emerging from his grave blazing with fire, with a chain around his neck which he dragged. He said: 'O servant of Allah, sprinkle (water), O servant of Allah, sprinkle!' By Allah, I do not know whether he recognized me by my name or as people call me. Then another came out and said: 'O servant of Allah, do not sprinkle,' then he pulled the chain and returned him to his grave."

(And) Ibn Abi al-Dunya said, and my father related to me, and Musa ibn Dawud related to us, and Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah from his father, who said: "While a rider was travelling between Makkah and Madinah, he passed by a cemetery, and there was a man who had come out of his grave blazing with fire, shackled in iron. He said: 'O servant of Allah, sprinkle, O servant of Allah, sprinkle, O servant of Allah, sprinkle!' And another came out following him and said: 'O servant of Allah, do not sprinkle, O servant of Allah, do not sprinkle.' The rider fainted, and his mount turned aside with him to al-ʿArj. In the morning his hair had turned white, and it was reported to ʿUthman, who forbade a man to travel alone."

(And) it is mentioned from the hadith of Sufyan: Hadathana Dawud ibn Shapur from Abu Qaza'ah, who said: "We passed by some of the waters between us and Basra, and we heard the braying of a donkey. We said to them: 'What is this braying?' They said: 'This is a man who was among us, whose mother used to speak to him about something, and he would say to her: "Bray your braying!" When he died, this braying was heard from his grave every night.'"

(Also) mentioned from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, who said: "There was a man from the people of Madinah, and he had a sister in a district of Madinah. She fell ill, and he used to visit her to attend to her. Then she died and he buried her. When he returned he recalled that he had forgotten something in the grave that he had with him, so he sought help from a man of his companions," he said:

"We dug up the grave and found that item. He said to the man: 'Step aside until I look at my sister's condition.'
