Yusuf said to him: "Tell Murthid what you saw." He said: "I was a young man who had committed these obscenities. When the plague struck, I said: 'I will go out to one of these frontier posts.' Then I decided to dig graves. One night, between maghrib and 'isha', I had dug, and I was leaning on the dirt of another grave, when a funeral of a man was brought and buried in that grave, and they leveled it over him. Then two white birds came from the west, like two camels, until one of them landed at his head and the other at his feet. Then they stirred him up, then one of them descended into the grave and the other remained at its edge. I came and sat on the edge of the grave, and I was a man whom nothing could fill. He said: I heard him say: 'Are you not the one who visits your in-laws in two dyed garments, dragging them in arrogance, strutting in pride?' He said: 'I am weaker than that.' He said: He struck him a blow, and the grave filled until water and oil overflowed. Then he returned and repeated the words to him until he had struck him three blows, each time saying that and mentioning that the grave overflows with water and oil. He said: Then he raised his head, looked at me, and said: 'Look where he sits, by the leave of Allah.' He said: Then he struck the side of my face and I fell. I remained that night until morning. He said: Then I began to look at the grave, and it was in its original state."

This water and oil, in the eye of the beholder, is in reality fire blazing for the dead, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) informed about the Dajjal, that he comes with water and fire; the fire is cold water, and the water is blazing fire.

(And) Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned that a man asked Abu Ishaq al-Fazari about the grave-robber (nabbash): "Is there repentance for him?" He said: "Yes, if his intention is sound and Allah knows his truthfulness." The man said: "I used to dig up graves, and I would find people whose faces were turned away from the qibla." Al-Fazari had no answer on this, so he wrote to al-Awza'i informing him of this. Al-Awza'i wrote back to him: "His repentance is accepted if his intention is sound and Allah knows the truthfulness of his heart. As for his saying that he found people whose faces were turned away from the qibla: those are people who died upon other than the Sunnah."

(And) Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: 'Abd al-Mu'min ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa al-Qaysi told me that it was said to a grave-robber who repented: "What is the most wondrous thing you saw?" He said: "I dug up a man who was nailed with nails all over his body, with a large nail in his head and another in his feet."

(And) it was said to another grave-robber: "What is the most wondrous thing you saw?" He said: "I saw a human skull into which lead had been poured."

(He said) It was said to another grave-robber: "What was the cause of your repentance?" He said: "Most of those I used to dig up, I saw them with faces turned away from the qibla."

(I say) My companion Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Musab al-Sulami, who was among the best of Allah's servants and who sought to be truthful, told me: A man came to the market of the blacksmiths in Baghdad and sold small nails, two-headed nails. The blacksmith took them and began to heat them, but they would not soften for him, until he was unable to strike them. He searched for the seller and found him, and said: "From where do you have these nails?"

He said: "I found them." He kept at him until he informed him that he had found an open grave in which were the bones of a dead person strung together with these nails. He said: "I tried to remove them but could not, so I took a stone and broke his bones and gathered them." He said: "I too saw those nails." I asked him: "What is their description?" He said: "A small nail with two heads."

(He said) Ibn Abi al-Dunya also said, and it was related to me from Abi ibn Jarish from his mother, who said: When Abu Ja'far dug the trench of Kufa, the people moved their dead, and we saw a young man from among those around us biting his own hand.

(And) it is related from Simak ibn Harb, who said: Abu al-Darda' passed among the graves and said: "How quiet your exteriors are, while within you are calamities."

(And) Thabit al-Bunani said: "While I was walking in the graveyards, I heard a voice behind me saying: 'O Thabit, do not be deceived by their silence, for how many a distressed one is among them.' I turned around and saw no one."

(And) al-Hasan passed by a graveyard and said: "What an army they are, how quiet they are, and how many distressed ones are among them."

(And) Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned that 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said to Maslamah ibn 'Abd al-Malik: "O Maslamah, who buried your father?" He said: "My master, so-and-so." He said: "And who buried al-Walid?" He said: "My master, so-and-so." He said: "I will tell you what was told to me: When they buried your father al-Walid, placing them in their graves, and he went to loosen the shroud from them, he found their faces had been turned around onto their necks. So, O Maslamah, when I die, search for my face and look: whether what befell the people has befallen me, or whether I have been spared from that." Maslamah said: "When 'Umar died, I placed him in his grave, and I touched his face, and it was in its place."

(And) Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from one of the early generations (salaf): "A daughter of mine died, and I lowered her into the grave. I went to adjust the bricks, and found that she had been turned away from the qibla. I was greatly grieved by this, and I saw her in a dream, and she said: 'O father, you were grieved by what you saw, for most of those around me are turned away from the qibla.'" He said: It seems she meant those who died persisting in major sins.

(And) 'Amr ibn Maymun said: I heard 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz say: "I was among those who lowered al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik into his grave, and I saw his knees gathered up against his neck." His son said: "My father lived, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" She said: "Your father was hastened, by the Lord of the Ka'bah," so 'Umar took warning from it after him.

(And) 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said to Yazid ibn al-Muhallab when he appointed him over Iraq: "O Yazid, fear Allah, for when I placed al-Walid in his tomb, he was kicking in his shroud."

(And) Yazid ibn Harun said: Hisham ibn Hassan reported from Wasil, client of Abu 'Uyaynah, from 'Umar ibn Zahdam, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Mahmud, who said: I was sitting with Ibn 'Abbas when a group came and said: "We set out as pilgrims, and with us was a companion of ours. When we arrived at al-Saffah, he died, so we prepared him, then went and dug a grave for him and dug a niche (lahd) for him. When we finished the niche, we found a black figure had filled the niche. We dug another for him, and there it was, filling that one too. We dug yet another, and there it was." Ibn 'Abbas said: "That is the chain with which he was shackled. Go, bury him in one of them. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if you dug the whole earth you would find him in it." So we went and placed him in one of them. When we returned, we brought his belongings to his family with us, and we said to his wife: "What did your husband used to do?" She said: "He used to sell food, and he would take each day his family's sustenance from it, then lend the surplus, the same amount, and throw it into it."

(And) Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, who said: Abu Ishaq, the companion of al-Shat, told me: I was called to a dead man to wash him. When I uncovered the cloth from his face, there was a snake coiled around his throat, and he described its thickness. I went out and did not wash him. It was reported that he used to revile the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them.

(And) Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from Sa'id ibn Khalid ibn Yazid al-Ansari, from a man of Basra who used to dig graves, who said: One day I dug a grave and placed my head close to it, and two women came to me in a dream. One of them said: "O servant of Allah, I beg you by Allah to turn this woman away from us and not let her be our neighbor." I woke up in alarm, and behold, the funeral of a woman had been brought. I said: "The grave is behind you," and I turned them away from that grave. When it was night, I saw the two women in my dream, and one of them said: "May Allah reward you with good on our behalf, for you have turned away a great evil from us." I said: "Why does your companion not speak to me as you speak to me?" She said: "This one died without a will, and it is right that whoever dies without a will should not speak until the Day of Resurrection."

These reports, and their multiples, and multiples of multiples, which this book cannot contain, are among what Allah, glorified is He, has shown some of His servants of the punishment of the grave and its bliss by direct witness.

As for dream visions, if we were to mention them they would fill several volumes. Whoever wishes to examine them should consult the book *al-Manamat* of Ibn Abi al-Dunya, and the book *al-Bustan* of al-Qayrawani, and other books containing such material. Yet the heretics (malahidah) and the zindiqs have nothing but denial of what they have not encompassed in knowledge.

The Seventh Matter: Allah, exalted is He, brings about in this world what is more wondrous than that. Gabriel used to descend upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and appear to him as a man, speaking to him with speech that he heard, while whoever was beside the Prophet (ﷺ) did not see or hear him. Likewise with other prophets. Sometimes revelation came to him like the ringing of a bell, and no one else present heard it. The jinn speak and converse with raised voices among us while we do not hear them. The angels used to strike the disbelievers with whips, strike their necks and shout at them, while the Muslims beside them did not see them or hear their speech. Allah, exalted is He, has veiled the children of Adam from much that He does in the earth while they are among them. Gabriel used to recite to the Prophet (ﷺ) and review the Qur'an with him while those present did not hear it.

How could one who knows Allah, glorified is He, and affirms His power find it strange that He should bring about events whose sight and sound He withholds from some of His creatures, out of wisdom and mercy toward them, since they cannot bear to see and hear them? The absent one is weaker in sight and hearing than to endure witnessing the punishment of the grave. Many of those whom Allah caused to witness it fainted and lost consciousness and never enjoyed life again for a time, and some had the veil of their heart lifted and died. So how can it be deemed strange in divine wisdom that a veil be lowered which prevents accountable beings from witnessing that, until the veil is lifted and they see it and witness it directly?

Furthermore, a servant is able to remove mercury and mustard seed from the eye and chest of a dead person and then return them swiftly. How then would the King be unable to do it, and how would He who is over all things powerful be unable? How would His power be incapable of keeping them in his eyes and on his chest so they do not fall? Is measuring the matter of the barzakh by what people observe in this world anything but pure ignorance and error, a denial of the Most Truthful of the truthful, and a belittling of the Lord of the worlds? That is the utmost of ignorance and injustice.

If one of us can widen a grave ten, a hundred cubits and more in length, breadth and depth, and conceal its widening from people, and let whomever he wishes see it, how then would the Lord of the worlds be unable to widen it for whom He wills, and conceal that from the eyes of the children of Adam, so that the children of Adam see it as narrow, while it is the most spacious thing, the most fragrant, the greatest in radiance and light, and they do not see that.

The essence of the matter: this spaciousness, narrowness, radiance, greenness and fire are not of the kind known in this world. Allah, glorified is He, only makes the children of Adam witness in this abode what is in it and from it. As for what belongs to the Hereafter, the veil is lowered over it, so that belief and faith in it may be a cause of their felicity. When the veil is lifted from them, it becomes direct witnessing. If the dead were placed among the people, it would not be impossible for the two angels to come to him and question him without those present perceiving it, and he would answer them without those present hearing his speech, and they would strike him without those present seeing his being struck. One of us sleeps beside his companion and is punished in sleep, struck and in pain, while the one awake has no knowledge of that at all, though the trace of the blow and the pain has passed into his body.

It is among the greatest ignorance to deem it unlikely that the angel splits the earth and the stone, when Allah has made them for him like air for the bird. That the bodies' density blocks them does not imply that it blocks the subtle spirits from passing through. Is this anything but the worst of faulty analogies? By this and its like the Messengers, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them, were denied.

The Eighth Matter: It is not impossible that the spirit be returned to the crucified, the drowned and the burned, though we are unaware of it, because that return is a different kind from the familiar one. Thus the fainted, the speechless and the dazed are alive, their spirits are with them, and they are unaware of their life. For one whose parts have been scattered, it is not impossible for He who is over all things powerful to make the spirit connected to those parts despite their distance and nearness, and for those parts to have some perception of pain and pleasure. Since Allah, exalted is He, has given inanimate things perception and awareness by which they glorify their Lord, and stones fall from fear of Him, mountains and trees prostrate to Him, and pebbles and water and plants glorify Him, Allah says: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾.

If glorification were merely their indicating their Creator, He would not have said: ﴿but you do not understand their glorification﴾, since anyone who understands their indication of their Creator would understand it. He says: ﴿Indeed, We subjected the mountains to glorify with Him at evening and sunrise﴾, and indication of the Creator is not restricted to these two times. Likewise His saying: ﴿O mountains, repeat praise with Him﴾, and indication is not restricted to His alone. Whoever says that "ta'wib" means the return of echo has lied against Allah, for that occurs for every sounding thing. He says: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the creatures, and many of mankind﴾. Indication of the Creator is not restricted to many of mankind. He has also said: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight? Each has known its prayer and its glorification﴾. This is genuine prayer and glorification, known to Allah, even if the ignorant deniers reject it. He, exalted is He, has informed about stones that some of them move from their place and fall from fear of Him. He informed that the earth and the heaven gave Him leave, and that their saying that means they listened to His speech, and that He addressed them and they heard His address and answered well. He said to them: ﴿Come willingly or unwillingly.﴾ They said: ﴿We come willingly.﴾

The Companions used to hear the glorification of food while it was being eaten, and they heard the moaning of the dry trunk in the mosque. If these bodies have sensation and perception, then bodies in which there was life and spirit are more deserving of it. Allah, glorified is He, has shown His servants in this abode the full restoration of life to a body from which the spirit had departed: it spoke, walked, ate, drank, married and had children. [He showed them that in the case of] those who left their homes in thousands fearing death, to whom Allah said: "Die," then He gave them life; or like the one who passed by a town fallen upon its roofs; he said: "How will Allah bring this to life after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him, and said: "How long have you remained?" He said: "I have remained a day or part of a day."

And like the murdered man of the Children of Israel, or like those who said to Moses: ﴿We will not believe you until we see Allah plainly﴾. Then Allah caused them to die, then raised them after their death; and like the People of the Cave, and the story of Abraham with the four birds. If He restored complete life to these bodies after they had grown cold with death, how could His overwhelming power be incapable of returning to them, after their death, a life that is not permanent, by which He decides what He commands regarding them, questions them through it, and punishes them or bestows bliss upon them according to their deeds? Is denying that anything but mere denial, obstinacy and rejection? And success is from Allah.

[Section: The Qur'an's not mentioning the punishment of the grave]

This is the question of the questioner: What is the wisdom in the punishment of the grave not being mentioned in the Qur'an, despite the great need to know it and believe in it, so that one might be warned and guard against it? The answer is in two ways: a summary and a detailed one.

As for the summary: Allah, glorified is He, sent down to His Messenger two revelations and obligated His servants to believe in both and act upon what is in them: the Book and the Wisdom. Allah says: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and the Wisdom﴾. He says: ﴿It is He who raised among the unlettered a messenger from among them, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and the Wisdom﴾. He says: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and the Wisdom﴾.

The Book is the Qur'an, and the Wisdom is the Sunnah, by the consensus of the early generations. What the Messenger reported from Allah must be believed and affirmed just as the Lord, exalted is He, reported it through the tongue of His Messenger. This is a principle agreed upon among the people of Islam and not denied except by one who is not among them.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I have been given the Book and its like along with it."

And as for the detailed answer: the bliss and punishment of the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection) are mentioned in the Qur'an in more than one place.

Among them is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels stretch out their hands, [saying], "Release your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and for being arrogant toward His signs."﴾ This is an address to them at the time of death, and the angels, who are truthful, have informed that at that moment they will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation. Had that been postponed for them until the end of the world, it would not be correct to say to them, "Today you will be recompensed."

Among them also is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they schemed, and there befell the people of Pharaoh an evil punishment. The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening; and on the day the Hour appears, [it will be said], "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾
Here He mentions the punishment of both abodes explicitly, admitting of no other meaning.

(Among them) the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck senseless. The Day their plotting will not avail them at all, nor will they be aided. And indeed, for those who have wronged is a punishment besides that, but most of them do not know.﴾ This may be taken to mean their punishment by killing and other means in this world, and it may be taken to mean their punishment in the barzakh, which is more apparent, because many of them died without being punished in this world. It may also be said, and this is more apparent: whoever of them died was punished in the barzakh, and whoever remained was punished in this world by killing and other means. So it is a warning of their punishment both in this world and in the barzakh.

(Among them) the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And We will surely make them taste a punishment nearer than the greater punishment, that perhaps they will return.﴾
Some scholars, among them Abdullah ibn Abbas, have cited this verse as evidence for the punishment of the grave, though there is something to be said about using it as proof, because this is a punishment in this world sought to bring about their return from disbelief, and this would not have been hidden from the scholar of the Ummah and interpreter of the Qur'an. Rather, his deep understanding of the Qur'an and the precision of his comprehension of it led him to derive from it the punishment of the grave. For He, glorified is He, informed that for them there are two punishments, a nearer and a greater. He informed that He makes them taste part of the nearer so that they may return, which shows that a remainder of the nearer punishment is left for them, by which they are punished after the punishment of this world. This is why He said "from the nearer punishment" and did not say "We will make them taste the nearer punishment." So reflect on it.

This is like the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Then an opening to the Fire is made for him, and its heat and hot wind reach him," and he did not say, "its heat and hot wind reach him" (in full). For what reaches him is some of that, and most of it remains for him. What the enemies of Allah tasted in this world is part of the punishment, and there remains for them what is greater than it.

(Among them) the saying of Allah: ﴿Then why, when [the soul] reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on, and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see — then why not, if you are not to be taken to account, [why] do you not return it, if you should be truthful? And as for if he was among those brought near [to Allah], then rest and bounty and a garden of pleasure. And as for if he was among the companions of the right, then, "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right." And as for if he was among the deniers, the misguided, then a welcome of boiling water and burning in Hellfire. Indeed, this is the true certainty. So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great.﴾

Here He mentions the states of the souls at death, and at the beginning of the surah He mentioned their states on the Great Day of Return. He placed this before that, as the end is placed first for emphasis, since it is more important and more fitting to mention. He divided them at death into three categories, just as He divided them in the Hereafter into three categories.

(Among them) the saying of Allah: ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]. So enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise.﴾
The predecessors differed about when this is said to it. One group said it is said to it at death, and the apparent wording agrees with them, for it is an address to the soul that has been separated from the body and has left it. The Prophet (ﷺ) explained this in his saying in the hadith of al-Bara' and others: "It is said to it, 'Go out, well-pleased and pleasing to Him.'" A full elaboration of this will come in the question where the resting place of souls in the barzakh is mentioned, God willing. His saying, "So enter among My servants," corresponds to the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "O Allah, the Highest Companion."

When you reflect on the hadiths about the punishment and bliss of the grave, you will find them a detailed explanation and elaboration of what the Qur'an indicates. And success is from Allah.

Know that the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunna wa'l-Jama'a is that faith (iman) increases and decreases.

Likewise, God's guardianship (wilaya) of His servant is in proportion to his faith. God Most High says: ﴿And God is the Protector of the believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 68].

And God Most High says: ﴿God is the Protector of those who believe﴾ [al-Baqara: 257].

Likewise, His special companionship (ma'iyya khassa) is for the people of faith, as God Most High says: ﴿And that God is with the believers﴾ [al-Anfal: 19].

So when faith weakens and diminishes, the servant's share of God's guardianship and His special companionship is according to his share of faith.

Likewise, complete victory and support belong only to the people of complete faith. God Most High says: ﴿Indeed We shall surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir: 51].

And He says: ﴿So We strengthened those who believed against their enemy, and they became the ones who prevailed﴾ [al-Saff: 14].

Thus, whoever's faith is deficient, his share of victory and support is deficient. This is why, when a servant is afflicted with a calamity in himself or his wealth, or when his enemy is given power over him, it is only because of his sins, either by abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act, which is itself a deficiency in his faith.

By this, the difficulty that many people raise regarding God's words ﴿And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ [al-Nisa': 141] is removed.

Many of them answer it by saying that He will not give them a way over them in the Hereafter, and others answer that He will not give them a way over them in argument (al-hujja).

The verified position (al-tahqiq) is that these verses are of the same kind, and that the absence of a way (for the enemy) applies to the people of complete faith. When faith weakens, their enemy gains over them a way in proportion to what they have lost of their faith. They themselves gave their enemies a way over them by what they abandoned of obedience to God Most High.

Thus the believer is mighty, dominant, supported, victorious, protected, and defended in his essence wherever he is, even if all the people of the earth gather against him, provided he upholds the reality of faith and its obligations, outwardly and inwardly. God Most High said to the believers: ﴿And do not weaken or grieve, for you will be superior if you are believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 139].

And God Most High said: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace while you are the superior, and God is with you and will not deprive you of your deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 35].

This guarantee is by means of their faith and their deeds, which are among the soldiers of God, by which He protects them. He does not separate them from these deeds or cut them off from them so as to nullify them for them, just as He causes the deeds of the disbelievers and hypocrites to perish, since those deeds were for other than Him and did not conform to His command.

As for the second position, in which error occurred: many people think that the people of the true religion will always be humiliated, subdued and defeated in this world, in contrast to those who part from them to another path and another obedience. Such people do not trust God's promise to support His religion and His servants. Rather, they either restrict that to one group rather than another, or to one time rather than another, or they make it conditional on God's will, even if they do not state it explicitly.

This is from a lack of trust in the promise of God Most High, and from a misunderstanding of His Book.

God, glorified is He, has made clear in His Book that He supports the believers in this world and the Hereafter.

God Most High said: ﴿Indeed We shall surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir: 51].

And God Most High said: ﴿And whoever takes God, His Messenger, and those who believe as allies, then indeed the party of God, they are the victorious﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 56].

And God Most High said: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger are among the most humiliated. God has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers"﴾ [al-Mujadila: 20-21].

This is abundant in the Qur'an.

He, glorified is He, has also made clear in it that whatever calamity, or enemy's gaining power, or defeat, or other such affliction befalls the servant, it is because of his sins.

Thus God has made both premises clear in His Book. When you combine them, the reality of the matter becomes clear to you, the difficulty is entirely removed, and you become free of those cold impositions and far-fetched interpretations.

(Faidah)

Through seeking forgiveness (istighfar) obedience is completed, and through patience certainty in the promise is completed. God, glorified is He, has combined the two in His saying:

﴿So be patient, for indeed the promise of God is true. And ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.﴾ [Ghafir: 55].

God, glorified is He, has mentioned in His Book the stories of the prophets and their followers, and how He saved them through patience and obedience. Then He said:

﴿There is certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding.﴾ [Yusuf: 111].

Since the thing sought refuge from in Surah "Ha Mim, the Believer" is the evil of the disbelievers' disputing about His signs, and what follows from it in their actions that are seen with the eye, He said: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute about the signs of Allah without authority having come to them—there is nothing in their breasts but pride, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ [Ghafir: 56].

For since what is sought refuge from is their speech and their actions that are witnessed directly, He said: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾

And there is a thing sought refuge from that is not visible to us, for he (Iblis) and his offspring see us from where we cannot see them. Rather, it is known through faith and through the report of Allah and His Messenger.

(Fasl)

As for the argument from His saying, ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾, and the claim that what is meant is greatness of rank and nobility, not greatness of bulk, this is utterly corrupt. The word "creation" (khalq) here means the act of creating, as applied to the thing created itself, and this is among the most eloquent proofs for the Resurrection. That is, He who created the heavens and the earth, and whose creating of them is greater than your creation, how could your creation be beyond His power after you die, when He recreates you in a new creation? A parallel to this is His saying in Surah Yasin: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾

That is, the likes of these deniers. This is an argument that power encompasses both kinds (of creation), and that it is capable of both, so it is not permissible to restrict it to one of the two objects of power to the exclusion of the other. Likewise His saying, "The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind," means: He whose power is not frustrated by creating the upper and lower world, how could He be frustrated by creating mankind anew after He has caused them to die? There is in this no reference, in any way at all, to the rulings of the stars or to the influence of the planets.

As for His saying, ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain"﴾, there is no doubt that the creation of the heavens and the earth is among the greatest proofs of the existence of their Originator, of His perfect power, knowledge and wisdom, and of His sole lordship and oneness. Whoever equates this with the gnat and makes the lesson, the indication and the knowledge of the existence of the Lord, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, from both of them equal, has indeed been arrogant. God, glorified is He, only calls His servants to look and reflect upon His great creatures, because the sign of indication is manifest in them, the wondrous marvels of craftsmanship and wisdom are in them, and the field of thought and contemplation in their expanses is broad.

Indeed, ﴿In everything there is a sign that indicates He is One.﴾

But where is the sign and the indication in the creation of the upper and lower world compared with the creation of the louse, the flea and the bedbug?

How could a sound mind allow itself to equate them, and make the indication from this like the indication from the other?

God, glorified is He, only mentions among His creatures, as evidence of Himself, the most noble and the most manifest to the senses and the intellect, the clearest in indication and the most wondrous in craftsmanship, such as the heavens, the earth, the sun, the moon, night and day, the stars, the mountains, the clouds, the rain and other of His signs. He does not call His servants to reflect upon lice, fleas, gnats, bedbugs, dogs, insects and the like. Whatever is mentioned of such things is mentioned in the context of coining parables, to emphasize their lowliness and weakness, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides God will never create a fly, even if they gather together for it. And if the fly should snatch away from them something, they could not recover it from it.﴾

Here the fly is not mentioned in the context of proving the existence of the Creator, exalted is He. Likewise His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is not ashamed to strike an example, [even] of a gnat or what is above it.﴾ And likewise His saying: ﴿The example of those who take other than God as protectors is like the spider, which takes a home; and indeed, the weakest of homes is the home of the spider.﴾

So reflect on the context in which these lowly creatures are mentioned, and the context in which the great creatures are mentioned.

As for the saying of some of the speculative theologians (mutakallimun), the over-elaborate ones, that the indication of the occurrence of life in animal bodies is stronger than the indication of the heavens and the earth for the existence of the Creator, exalted is He, this claim rests on a corrupt premise: the affirmation of the indivisible atom (al-jawhar al-fard), and that the Creator's influence in the creation of the upper and lower world is the composition and assembling of those atoms, this particular assembly and composition being of a kind that is within the power of humans and others.

As for innovation and origination (al-ihdath wa'l-ikhtira'), none can do it except God. The doctrine of the indivisible atom, and the building of the origin and the Resurrection upon it, is among the corrupt principles of the theologians, which the majority of intelligent people have disputed.

They said: God's creating and originating of what He originates of the bodies of the world is the origination of their parts and essences, not merely the composition of separate atoms. Then, once their creation, making and origination are completed, what is now occurring is only their assembly and composition.

This is among the statements of the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah) which they innovated in Islam, and upon which they built the Resurrection and the origination of the world. So the enemies of Islam gained power over them, and they were unable to break them, because they had built the origin and the Resurrection upon a fanciful, imaginary matter. They thought that they could not establish the doctrine of the world's createdness and the re-creation of bodies except by it. Their opponents set forth very many arguments against the doctrine of the atom, and they themselves acknowledged the strength and soundness of many of them. This caused doubt to fall upon many of them regarding the matter of origin and Resurrection, since they had built it upon a crumbling precipice.

As for the leading scholars of Islam and its most accomplished theorists, they did not rely on this method, which they regarded as too weak and feeble to build upon it any part of the religion, let alone the createdness of the world and the re-creation of bodies. They relied only on the ways God, glorified is He, guided to in His Book: the origination of the very essence of animals and plants, the creation of the very self of the upper and lower world, and the origination of clouds, rain, winds and other bodies whose origination is witnessed in their very essences, not merely the origination of their composition and assembly. For those who affirm the atom, one does not witness that God originated in this world any of the atoms; rather He originated only their assembly and composition, even if His origination of their atoms was prior and earlier than that.

Now, what occurs is only accidents (a'rad) of gathering, separation, motion and rest, and these are the "modes of being" (akwan) in their view. Likewise the Resurrection: He, glorified is He, disperses the parts of the world, which is its annihilation, then reassembles and gathers them, and this is the Resurrection. These people needed to argue that the very person of the human and his atoms are created, since what is witnessed by the senses at all times is the occurrence of accidents in those atoms, from pure composition. They claimed that whatever God originates of clouds, rain, crops, fruits and animals, He originates in it only accidents, namely the gathering and dispersing of atoms that already existed. They claimed that no one knows the origination of any entity by witnessing or by necessity of reason, but only by inference.

The majority of intelligent people among the sects oppose these, and say that the Lord never ceases to originate entities, as the senses, reason and the Qur'an indicate. For bodies whose essences and parts are witnessed as originated, having not been dispersed atoms that then came together.

Whoever says otherwise has indeed been arrogant toward the senses and reason. For the fact that the human and the animal are created, originated, having come into being after not being, is a matter known necessarily to all people, and everyone knows that he came into being in his mother's womb after not existing, and that his very self came into being, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And I created you before, when you were nothing.﴾ This is not, in their view, something to be inferred; rather it is inferred from, as is the method of the Qur'an, for it made the origination and creation of man a proof, not something proven.

Their saying that what is originated is only accidents, and that it is composed of separate atoms, are two false claims. Rather, the origination of the very person and essence of the human is known, and the falsity of the indivisible atom is known. Even if the doctrine of the atom were sound, it would not be known except through hidden, subtle proofs, and so it would not be among the fundamentals of religion, nor even a premise in it. Their method therefore involves denying what is known, namely the origination of originated entities and their essences, and affirming what is not known but is in fact false, namely the indivisible atom. This is not the place to exhaust this question. The intended point is the discussion of his saying that the inference from the occurrence of life in the structure of the animal to the existence of the Creator is stronger than the indication of the composition of the celestial bodies, and that this is built upon this corrupt premise.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 40, verse 60:**

Supplication (*du'a'*, calling upon God) is of two kinds: supplication of worship (*du'a' 'ibadah*) and supplication of request (*du'a' mas'alah*). The one who worships is a supplicant, just as the one who asks is a supplicant. Both meanings have been given as the explanation of God's words ﴿Your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾.

It has been said: "Obey Me, I will reward you."

It has also been said: "Ask Me, I will give you." Both meanings were given as the explanation of God's words ﴿When My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the call of the caller when he calls upon Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 186].

The correct view is that supplication encompasses both types, and this is a term applied univocally (*mutawatti'*), not homonymously (*mushtarak*).

**[Supplication repels what is disliked]**

Likewise, supplication is among the strongest causes for repelling what is disliked and attaining what is sought. However, its effect may be withheld from it, either because of its weakness in itself, by being a supplication that God does not love due to the transgression it contains, or because of the weakness of the heart and its failure to turn to God and gather itself toward Him at the time of supplication. In that case it is like a very slack bow, from which the arrow leaves with only weak force. Or its effect may be withheld because of an obstacle to being answered: eating what is unlawful, wrongdoing, the rust of sins upon the hearts, and the dominance of heedlessness, desire and frivolity over them.

This is as in the *Mustadrak* of al-Hakim, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ): «Call upon God while you are certain of being answered.»

And: «Know that God does not accept supplication from a heart that is heedless and frivolous.» This is a beneficial medicine that removes the disease, but the heart's heedlessness toward God nullifies its strength, and likewise eating what is unlawful nullifies and weakens its strength.

As in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «O people, God is good and accepts only what is good, and God has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, saying: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds; indeed I am Knower of what you do﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 51], and He said: ﴿O you who have believed, eat of the good things We have provided you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 172].» Then he mentioned a man who prolongs the journey, disheveled and dusty, who stretches his hands to the sky, saying: "O Lord, O Lord," while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he is nourished with the unlawful. How then would he be answered?»

Abdullah ibn Ahmad mentioned in the *Kitab al-Zuhd* of his father: A calamity befell the Children of Israel, so they went out to a place of supplication. God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to their prophet: "Tell them: You go out to the open ground with impure bodies, and you raise to Me hands with which you have shed blood and filled your houses with the unlawful. Now, when My anger has intensified against you? You will only increase in distance from Me."

Abu Dharr said: "With supplication and righteousness, what is sufficient is what salt is sufficient for food."

Here there is a well-known question, which is: If the thing supplicated for has been decreed, then it must occur, whether the servant supplicates for it or not. And if it has not been decreed, it will not occur, whether the servant asks for it or not.

A group thought this question to be valid, so they abandoned supplication and said: "There is no benefit in it." These people, along with their extreme ignorance and misguidance, are self-contradictory, for consistently applying their doctrine necessitates the nullification of all causes. So it is said to one of them:

If satiety and quenching of thirst have been decreed for you, then they must occur, whether you eat or do not eat. And if they have not been decreed, they will not occur, whether you eat or do not eat.

And if a child has been decreed for you, then it must come, whether you have intercourse with a wife or a slave-woman or not. And if it has not been decreed, it will not come, so there is no need for marriage or concubinage, and so on.

Would any rational or human being say this? Rather, even the beasts are created to engage in the causes by which their sustenance and life are maintained. Thus animals are more intelligent and more perceptive than these people, who are like cattle, nay, they are even more astray.

Some of them became clever and said: "Occupying oneself with supplication is purely a matter of worship, for which God rewards the one who supplicates, without it having any effect on the thing sought in any way." For this clever one, there is no difference between supplication and refraining from it, in heart and tongue, regarding the effect on attaining what is sought. In their view, the connection of supplication to the outcome is like the connection of silence to it, and there is no difference.

Another group, cleverer than these, said: "Rather, supplication is a bare sign which God, glorified is He, has set as an indicator of the fulfilment of need. Whenever a servant is granted success in supplication, that is a sign for him and an indication that his need has been fulfilled. This is like when you see a black, cold cloud in the winter; that is evidence and a sign that it will rain."

They said: "Likewise is the ruling regarding acts of obedience and their reward, and disbelief and sins and their punishment. These are purely indicators of the occurrence of reward and punishment, not causes of them."

And likewise, in their view, breaking is with being broken, burning is with being burned, and killing is with death. None of these is a cause at all, and there is no connection between them and what follows from them, except a mere customary concomitance, not a causal influence. By this they opposed the senses, reason, the Law, human nature, and all the rest of the groups of rational people. Indeed, they made rational people laugh at them.

The correct view is that there is a third category, other than what the questioner mentioned, namely that this decreed matter was decreed with causes, and among its causes is supplication. It was not decreed bare of its cause, but it was decreed through its cause. Whenever the servant brings the cause, the decreed matter occurs, and whenever he does not bring the cause, the decreed matter does not occur. This is like how satiety and quenching of thirst were decreed through eating and drinking, a child was decreed through intercourse, the growth of crops was decreed through sowing seed, the departure of an animal's soul was decreed through slaughter. Likewise, entry into Paradise was decreed through deeds, and entry into Hell through deeds. This category is the truth, and it is what the questioner was deprived of and was not granted success in.

**Supplication is among the strongest causes**

Accordingly, supplication is among the strongest causes. So when the thing sought is decreed to occur through supplication, it is not valid to say: "There is no benefit in supplication," just as one does not say: "There is no benefit in eating, drinking, and all movements and actions." There is no cause more beneficial than supplication, nor more effective in attaining what is sought.

**'Umar seeks victory through supplication**

Since the Companions, may God be pleased with them, were the most knowledgeable of the Community about God and His Messenger (ﷺ), and the most learned in his religion, they were more upright than others in this cause, its conditions and its etiquette.

'Umar, may God be pleased with him, used to seek victory through it over his enemy. He was the greatest of his soldiers, and he used to say to his companions: "You are not victorious through numbers, but you are victorious from heaven." He also used to say: "I do not bear the concern of being answered, but the concern of supplication. If you are inspired to supplicate, then answer is with it." A poet took this meaning and versified it, saying:

*If you did not wish to grant what I hope for and seek*
*from the generosity of your two hands, you would not have taught me to ask.*

Whoever is inspired to supplicate, answer has been willed for him, for God, glorified is He, says: ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60], and He says: ﴿When My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the call of the caller when he calls upon Me﴾.

In the Sunan of Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «Whoever does not ask God, He will be angry with him.»

This shows that His pleasure lies in being asked and in obedience to Him. When the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, is pleased, then all good is in His pleasure, just as all calamity and misfortune are in His anger.

Imam Ahmad mentioned in the *Kitab al-Zuhd* a report: «I am God, there is no god but Me. When I am pleased, I bless, and there is no end to My blessing. When I am angry, I curse, and My curse reaches to the seventh generation of offspring.»

Reason, transmitted texts, human nature, and the experiences of nations, despite their differing kinds, religions and sects, all indicate that drawing near to the Lord of the worlds, seeking His good pleasure, and doing righteousness and kindness to His creation are among the greatest causes that bring every good. Their opposites are among the greatest causes that bring every evil. The blessings of God are not drawn down, nor His vengeance repelled, by anything like obedience to Him, drawing near to Him, and kindness to His creation.

**The connection of good and evil with action**

God, glorified is He, has linked the attainment of goods in this world and the Hereafter, and the attainment of joy in this world and the Hereafter, in His Book, to deeds, in the manner of the reward being linked to the condition, the effect to its cause, and the caused to its cause. This appears in the Qur'an more than a thousand times.

In sum, the Qur'an from beginning to end is explicit in the ordering of reward with good and evil, and of the cosmic and legislative rulings, to causes. Indeed, it orders the rulings of this world and the Hereafter, and their benefits and harms, upon causes and deeds.

Whoever comprehends this matter and reflects upon it with due reflection benefits from it to the utmost, and does not rely upon destiny out of ignorance, incapacity, negligence and neglect. Otherwise his trust becomes incapacity, and his incapacity becomes trust. Rather, the complete jurist is the one who repels destiny with destiny, averts destiny with destiny, and counters destiny with destiny. Indeed, it is impossible for a person to live except in this way, for hunger, thirst, cold, and all kinds of fears and dangers are part of destiny.

All of creation is heedless of repelling this destiny with destiny. Likewise, whoever God grants success and inspires with his right guidance repels the destiny of otherworldly punishment with the destiny of repentance, faith and righteous deeds. This is the exact counterpart of the destiny that frightens in this world, and what opposes it. The Lord of the two abodes is one, His wisdom is one, and some of it does not contradict another part, nor does some of it nullify another. This matter is among the most noble of questions for one who knows its worth and observes it as it should be observed. And God is the One sought for help.

**(Benefit)**

One of the scholars heard a man supplicating for well-being, and said to him:

"Sir, use medicines and supplicate for well-being. For if God has made a path to well-being, which is treatment, and you supplicate for well-being, His reply may well be: 'I have granted you well-being through what I made and placed as a cause for well-being.' This is like a man who has a breach between his field and the water, through which water enters to irrigate his crop, and who then begins to pray and ask for water for his crop, seeking rain, although he is able to open that breach to water his crop. That is neither good in the Law nor in reason. This is only because the giving has been preceded by the giving of causes. God gives through one of two paths: He may give through a cause and without a cause, and through a cause so that by it there may become manifest what His craftsmanship has poured out and what He has deposited in His creatures of powers, natures and benefits. His giving without a cause makes clear to the servants that His power does not depend on an intermediary in His action. So when you supplicate for well-being, then seize what He has given you of resources and provisions. If they reach you through it, well and good; otherwise, seek as one who has become bankrupt seeks his due, and turn to the Mine, as the Master of creation said: 'O God, this is my portion of what I possess, so do not blame me for what You possess and I do not.'"

I say: This is a fine statement, and more complete than it is that one should expend the causes and ask as one who relies on nothing at all.

People in this station are of four kinds:

- The most incapable is the one who neither expends the cause nor increases his seeking. This is the most contemptible of creatures.

- The second is the opposite: the wisest of people is the one who relies upon the causes God established as leading to the sought thing, and yet asks as one who relies on no cause at all, rather as a bankrupt, wretched person, who has no stratagem or means.

- The third is one who employs the causes, directs his resolve to them, and limits his view to them. Although he has a share of what God has ordained through them, it is deficient and cut off. He faces afflictions and obstacles. It is attained only after toil, and once attained it is quick to vanish and swift to depart, leaving him no tawhid, no knowledge, and no means of opening the door between him and his Worshipped One.

- The fourth is the opposite: a man who casts the causes behind his back, and turns to seeking, supplication and imploring. This is praiseworthy in one situation and blameworthy in another, and in some situations it is shameful. It is praiseworthy when those causes are not commanded, for in them there is harm to his religion. So if he abandons them and turns to asking, imploring and humbling himself before God, it is praiseworthy. It is blameworthy when the causes are commanded, and he abandons them and turns to supplication. Like one whom the enemy has besieged, and who was commanded to fight, but abandons fighting and turns to supplication and humility that God turn the enemy away from him. Or like one overcome by thirst, who is able to take water, but leaves it and turns to asking God to quench his thirst. Or like one who is able to seek lawful treatment, but leaves it and turns to asking for well-being. And there are similar cases.

The matter becomes unclear regarding causes whose consequences are not evident to him, which contain some ambiguity, and which have necessary consequences he may be unable to bear, or from which there may arise what returns to diminish his religion. This is a place of ambiguity and danger. The judge in all of this is the command. If it remains hidden, then there is istikharah (prayer for guidance), and the command of God lies beyond that.
